Native Object Logic

U NOL

U NOL is shorthand for Universal Native Object Logic. "U" is written separately from "NOL" to indicate that NOL is the subject and U is the modifier (i.e. it is native object logic which is universal, as opposed to something like UN OL which would indicate object logic which is universal and native).

Native object logic is presumably referring to the logic (a manner of thinking, the operation of the mind) which is native (inbuilt, first-order) to an object (thing which exists). This would be similar to what is commonly referred to as instinct, though instinct implies something closer to a subconscious reaction or behavior, whereas NOL would refer to the intrinsic nature of the operation of a thing's mind. In other words, how the thing must think due to the structure of its being.

He suggests that the concept of "be here now" (meaning something like living in the present and being aware of your surroundings) is a form of NOL which is universal among all objects (e.g. dogs, cats, rats). I suspect when he says "Oh yeah, every dog cat rat knows their birthday," he is being sarcastic. The overall message seems to be that the idea of time is bad ("A Gregorian braintrap," "[days of the week] has nothing to do with your life," "You got ticks. You need me," etc.). In his view, all other animals do not have a notion of time, and they are better off for it.
